summary: An announcement about the ARPA Network Control Center at BBN. It was now staffed 24 hours a day, every day, so users should call about IMP, TIP or network problems at any time. It gives a new phone number and asks sites to post it near their IMPs.

plainLanguage.summary: The Network Control Center announced that it was staffed 24 hours a day, every day. The notice gives a new phone number and asks sites to keep it visible near their IMPs.

subtitle: Round-the-clock Network Control Center coverage and contact details

tldr.problem: People reporting network problems had sometimes encountered busy signals when calling the Network Control Center.
tldr.mechanism: The notice says the NCC was now staffed at all times and gives a new phone number for contacting it.
tldr.outcome: Sites were asked to post the new number near their IMPs and report busy signals when they reached an operator.

today: RFC 356 is an operational notice about Network Control Center staffing and contact information. It records the phone number and procedures announced in June 1972.

sections.title: NCC Coverage
sections.content: The Network Control Center operations staff had been expanded so that the NCC was staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Sites were asked to contact it at any time about IMP, TIP or network problems.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites could call the Network Control Center at any time to report problems with an IMP, TIP or the network.

sections.title: New Telephone Number
sections.content:
The new NCC number was (617) 661-0100. The notice asks sites to post it near their IMPs and tell people who may need to call. The old number would continue to operate for a while.

If a caller received a busy signal, the notice says to keep trying and tell the operator about the busy signal after reaching them.
sections.plainLanguage: Post the new NCC number near the equipment. If the line is busy, keep trying and tell the operator when you get through.

sections.title: Written Contact
sections.content: The RFC provides a mailing address for written messages to the ARPA Network Control Center at Bolt Beranek and Newman Inc. in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It also lists field service managers and site contacts for information purposes.
sections.plainLanguage: The notice also gives a mailing address for the Network Control Center. It lists people who were copied on the announcement.
